target_customer: Software developers choosing open-source libraries, monetized via developer-facing products or sponsors (not stated)
problem: Developers face millions of open-source packages and need ratings, downloads and commit data to choose one.
business_model: Free discovery platform with planned monetization; the team later said it never became a large profitable business

founders.name: Lior Grossman
founders.background_notes: YC page lists no bio. Software Engineering Daily interviewed him in November 2020.

exit.reason: A message from the team on Product Hunt says it could not grow Openbase into a large profitable company and chose to close it in 2023.

competitors.name: GitHub and package registries (npm, PyPI, Maven)
competitors.what: Default places to browse and search packages, with limited categories and filters

technical_complexity.rationale: Aggregating and ranking data for 1.5 million JavaScript packages with beta Python and Go support is standard data engineering with some scale challenges.

defensibility.rationale: Reviews and rankings could accumulate, but the underlying metrics were public and rivals such as Libraries.io existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source records an incumbent copying it; the team said in 2023 that it could not build a large profitable business.

market_need_then: Developers faced millions of packages; VentureBeat in January 2021 framed the pain as choosing among them and positioned Openbase as the Yelp for open source packages.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positioned as the Yelp for open source packages

branding.brand_signature: Yelp for open source packages framing
branding.community_and_virality: Had a Product Hunt listing and a Software Engineering Daily episode (November 2020), and a dev.to discussion; no merch or fan communities found.

brand_strength.rationale: Press from VentureBeat and TechCrunch plus a podcast, but the name is generic and shares words with other Open* products; no iconic assets found.

outcome_analysis: Openbase raised a 3.65M dollar seed in January 2021 and gained developer attention as the Yelp for open source packages. The team said in 2023 it could not grow it into a large profitable company and closed it, so the stated cause is lack of a profitable business. The labels weak willingness to pay and market too small are judgments from that statement, since developers used free alternatives.
notes: Seed amount is 3.65M per the TechCrunch snippet and 3.6M in its headline; Startupintros says 4M. A later 2.44M seed in April 2022 rests on a single database (BounceWatch); another database cites 6.21M total, which suggests it may be consistent with the two rounds. The direct TechCrunch URL returned 404 so the search result link was cited. Competitor evidence is dated January 2021, about five months after the batch. Company website was not live (YC says discontinued 2023), so no site fetch was possible.
